issues.t: Lower intake manifold gasket coolant leak
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell after driving, coolant seeping near the top of the engine, overheating, or in bad cases milky, light-brown oil on the dipstick.
issues.why: The original plastic-type lower intake gaskets on these GM V6 engines break down over time and let coolant escape, either outside the engine or into the oil.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and temperature gauge. Have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and replace the gaskets with the revised metal-frame type before coolant mixes with the oil and damages the bearings.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping, harsh shifts or failure
issues.sym: Hard or erratic shifts, slipping, flaring revs between gears, being stuck in one gear, or a check engine light with transmission codes.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic in these cars commonly suffers from a worn pressure control solenoid and internal wear. GM issued bulletins for slipping, harsh shifts and shudder with codes like P0748 and P1811.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the fluid checked. Catching a bad pressure control solenoid early can avoid a full rebuild; slipping that continues usually means internal damage.

issues.t: Oil can drip onto the exhaust manifold and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Burning oil smell, smoke from under the hood, or oil on the rear exhaust manifold. In the worst case an engine fire, even when parked.
issues.why: Oil leaking from the valve cover area can drip onto the hot exhaust manifold. GM recalled these cars several times (09V-116 and later 15V-701) and the final fix replaces the front valve cover and gasket.
issues.next: Check for open recalls with your VIN and have the free repair done. Until then, park outside and away from buildings.

issues.t: Ignition key can be bumped out of Run (recall)
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving after the key or key ring is bumped, with loss of power steering and power brakes.
issues.why: The ignition switch can rotate out of the Run position with a heavy key ring or a knee bump. If that happens, the airbags may not deploy in a crash. GM recall 14V-400 covers it.
issues.next: Use only the key on its ring, with nothing heavy attached, and have the free recall repair done at a dealer.

issues.t: Ignition switch can turn off while driving (recall)
issues.sym: The car shuts off while driving, especially over bumps or if the key is bumped, and steering and braking suddenly get much harder.
issues.why: The key can move out of the Run position. With the ignition off, the airbags may not deploy and power steering and brakes are lost. GM recall 14V-355 covers these years.
issues.next: Remove heavy items from your key ring and get the free recall repair. If the engine shuts off, steer firmly to a safe stop.

issues.t: No-start with flashing security light (Passlock)
issues.sym: The engine cranks but will not start, or won't start at all, and the security light flashes or stays on. Often it will start after waiting 10 to 20 minutes.
issues.why: The Passlock anti-theft system loses the signal from the sensor in the ignition lock cylinder, usually due to a worn lock cylinder sensor or wiring, and shuts off fuel to the engine.
issues.next: Leave the key in On for about 10 minutes until the security light stops flashing, then try again. If it keeps happening, have a shop test the Passlock sensor and ignition cylinder wiring.

issues.t: Turn signals work only some of the time
issues.sym: Turn signals stop flashing or only work occasionally. Switching the hazard lights on and off often brings them back for a while.
issues.why: The hazard (4-way) switch in the dash wears internally. Because the turn signal circuit runs through it, a worn hazard switch breaks the turn signals too. Sometimes the steering column multifunction switch is at fault.
issues.next: Try cycling the hazard switch as a short-term fix and have the hazard switch replaced. It is a small part and a quick job.

issues.t: ABS and traction control lights on
issues.sym: The ABS and Service Traction System lights come on, sometimes on and off. Anti-lock braking may be disabled, and the ABS pump may run when it should not.
issues.why: A failed or damaged front wheel speed sensor or its wiring is the usual cause on these cars, and a worn hub bearing can upset the sensor. GM also issued bulletins for ABS pump and module faults.
issues.next: Normal brakes still work, but ABS may not. Have the ABS codes read to find which wheel sensor or wire is at fault.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hum or grinding
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed and changes when turning, or a loose feeling at the front wheel.
issues.why: The front hub bearing assemblies wear out, often around 70,000–140,000 miles. They are among the most-reported repairs for these cars.
issues.next: Have the wheels checked for play. A badly worn bearing can seize or let the wheel wobble, so do not ignore a growing noise.

issues.t: Power window drops or stops working
issues.sym: The window falls into the door, goes up crooked, makes grinding or popping noises, or won't move at all.
issues.why: The window regulator cables and plastic parts wear and break. It is a widely reported repeat repair on this car.
issues.next: Tape the glass up if it has dropped, and have the regulator (and motor if needed) replaced.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge jumps around, reads empty when it isn't, or the low-fuel chime sounds too early.
issues.why: The fuel level sensor inside the tank wears or gets coated by sulfur in fuel. GM issued bulletins for incorrect and fluctuating fuel gauges.
issues.next: Track your mileage between fill-ups so you don't run out. A shop can replace the sending unit in the fuel pump module.

issues.t: Clunk from the steering when turning
issues.sym: A clunk or pop felt through the steering wheel at low speed or when turning, often in parking lots.
issues.why: The intermediate steering shaft between the column and steering gear binds and releases. GM bulletins call for lubricating or replacing it.
issues.next: It is usually not dangerous, but have the front end checked so worn tie rods or ball joints aren't missed.

issues.t: Power steering cooler line or hose leak
issues.sym: Power steering fluid on the ground or engine, a whining pump, or heavier steering.
issues.why: The power steering cooler line can leak or split on V6 and V8 cars. GM ran a customer satisfaction campaign for it, and bulletins also cover leaking hoses.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for leaks. Ask a dealer if the GM campaign work was done; otherwise replace the leaking line.

issues.t: Brakes feel delayed on wet roads (recall)
issues.sym: When braking lightly on wet roads or after a car wash, the car does not slow down right away.
issues.why: Water on the brakes can briefly reduce braking until the pads dry. The cars were included in a 2001 GM brake campaign for this condition.
issues.next: Leave extra stopping distance in the rain, lightly brake after a car wash to dry the brakes, and ask a Chevrolet dealer if the campaign work was done on your car.

issues.t: Rough idle and misfire from clogged fuel injectors
issues.sym: Hard starting, rough idle, stumbling or chuggle, and a check engine light for misfire.
issues.why: Deposits build up on the fuel injectors on these V6 engines, and GM issued bulletins for clogged injectors and injector corrosion.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes checked. Injector cleaning helps in mild cases; replacement is needed if they keep acting up.

issues.t: Timing belt failure (3.4L DOHC)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly stops running and won't restart; it cranks faster than normal. There is often no warning.
issues.why: The Z34's twin-cam 3.4L uses a timing belt to drive the camshafts. If it isn't replaced on time it can snap, and on some years the valves can be damaged.
issues.next: If you don't know when the belt was last changed, have it replaced. If it has already broken, don't keep cranking the engine; have the valves checked first.

issues.t: A/C blows warm
issues.sym: Air from the vents isn't cold, the A/C works only some of the time, or the compressor is noisy.
issues.why: Compressor failures and refrigerant leaks are frequent repairs on this car. GM also put out a bulletin for weak A/C in hot, humid weather.
issues.next: Have a shop check pressures and look for leaks before simply recharging. A recharge alone often fails again if there is a leak.

issues.t: Engine stalls or dies while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving, often once warmed up, and may not restart right away.
issues.why: Owners trace this to failing camshaft or crankshaft position sensors, damaged sensor wiring, or in some cases the engine computer. Some cars took several tries to diagnose.
issues.next: Pull over safely. Have codes read right after it happens; ask the shop to check sensor wiring before replacing the computer.

issues.t: Intake manifold gasket leak (3.5L and 3.9L)
issues.sym: Coolant or oil seeping at the top of the engine, a dropping coolant level or an oil smell.
issues.why: The intake manifold gaskets on the newer 3.5L and 3.9L V6 can also leak with age and mileage.
issues.next: Keep an eye on fluid levels and have the leak confirmed before it causes overheating.

issues.t: Oil consumption (5.3L V8)
issues.sym: You need to add oil between changes, see blue smoke at startup, or get misfires and fouled spark plugs.
issues.why: GM's V8s with cylinder deactivation (Active Fuel Management) are known to burn oil, and GM issued oil consumption bulletins covering these engines.
issues.next: Check the oil level every fill-up. Ask a shop to do a GM oil consumption test; fixes range from a PCV or valley cover update to engine work.

issues.t: Clicking behind the dashboard
issues.sym: A repeated clicking or clattering from behind the dash, often after starting the car or changing temperature or vent settings.
issues.why: A small HVAC door actuator motor has stripped gears and keeps trying to move the door.
issues.next: It is not harmful, but the vents may stop switching. A shop can find and replace the faulty actuator.

issues.t: Rusted-out muffler and exhaust pipes
issues.sym: A louder exhaust, rattling underneath, or an exhaust smell.
issues.why: The muffler, resonator and pipes rust through, especially on cars from snowy states. Owners report it as a frequent repair.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected. Leaks near the cabin can let fumes inside, so fix them promptly.

issues.t: Repeat oil pan leak
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the car and an oily oil pan, even after a gasket was replaced.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for repeat oil pan leaks on these engines, calling for a revised repair.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and fixed with the updated procedure; keep the oil topped up.

issues.t: Instrument cluster gauges act up
issues.sym: The speedometer, tachometer, fuel or temperature gauge jumps around, sticks, or drops to zero, often while driving.
issues.why: The instrument cluster's circuit board or gauge motors fail. Owners usually fix it by replacing or repairing the cluster.
issues.next: Note that your speed and temperature readings can't be trusted. Have the cluster repaired or replaced.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may be missing a check pin (recall)
issues.sym: There is usually no sign at all.
issues.why: Some passenger airbags were built without a small check valve pin, which changes how hard the bag inflates. That can raise injury risk in a crash. GM recalled the cars (02V-329).
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free dealer repair done.
